page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.xlarge is an entry-tier virtual instance belonging to the shared burstable t5 family. Powered by the x86_64 architecture, it is configured with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The allocation consists of 4 vCPUs distributed across 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache specifications include 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 33 MB L3 cache pool.

The instance relies entirely on remote storage, providing no integrated local disk volumes. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned with the hardware profile. Acceleration hardware is not present, with zero GPUs included in the configuration.

Benchmark measurements indicate modest baseline compute capabilities consistent with a shared-core burstable model. The processor achieved 994.99 in stress-ng single-core tests and 4027.78 in multi-core tests, placing it in the lower quartile of compute benchmarks. Geekbench results follow this trend, reporting 806.0 for single-core and 2327.0 for multi-core performance. Memory throughput reached 28.92 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 26.44 GB/sec for writes. Database operations in PassMark scored 957.18, while Redis SET throughput recorded 4.15 million operations per second, reflecting the entry-level baseline of the burstable CPU profile.

From an efficiency standpoint, the ecs.t5-c1m4.xlarge delivers substantial memory capacity at low resource overhead by leveraging a burstable CPU throttling model. This makes the instance suitable for lightweight applications that experience intermittent traffic or periodic computational bursts. Tradeoffs include low sustained compute ceilings and constrained single-threaded performance. Recommended workloads include staging environments, continuous integration test runners, lightweight background workers, and low-traffic internal web services.
